subject.title: fix(openshell): bound sandbox readFile with size cap

question: Is a fixed 100 MiB maximum sandbox read the intended OpenShell compatibility boundary for existing users, and should it be enforced through the shared fs-safe read contract?
rationale: The cap is a user-visible fail-closed change for previously permitted large reads; the repository’s shared filesystem API can implement the mechanism, but maintainers must choose the permanent policy boundary.

options.title: Adopt the shared 100 MiB boundary
options.body: Confirm that OpenShell should reject sandbox reads above 100 MiB, replace the local chunk reader with fs-safe `root.read()` using that limit, and add focused proof.

options.title: Choose a different boundary
options.body: Specify another documented limit or compatibility approach before implementing it through the shared fs-safe API.

options.title: Pause the hardening change
options.body: Keep current behavior until the OpenShell compatibility and resource-budget policy is settled.

recommendation.title: Adopt the shared 100 MiB boundary
recommendation.body: Confirm that OpenShell should reject sandbox reads above 100 MiB, replace the local chunk reader with fs-safe `root.read()` using that limit, and add focused proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available adjacent-history candidate for the shared fs-safe contract, though direct OpenShell ownership could not be established from the available history.
